bibl.title: Amores
bibl.note: The scanned title identifies Tom. I despite the archive catalogue volume label. One-based viewer pages 113–114 have been inspected; source links are recorded in the facsimile.

normalization.p: Source wording, capitalization, contracted forms and punctuation retained. Typographic ligatures use constituent letters; quotation marks are represented schematically by curly quotes. OCR locates text but does not determine readings.

segmentation.p: Each l corresponds to a printed verse; n preserves the corpus verse identifier. Verses follow the source order, including any transposed couplets, rather than being silently reordered. Each line links to its existing annotation rectangle. Page breaks may occur within couplets. Source headings and running titles are encoded separately.

correction.p: Source readings are not silently replaced by a modern edition. Distinctive features are explained in notes for independent checking.

revisionDesc.change: Independently inspected all 44 actual source verses and every author note. Confirmed source wording, punctuation, marks, page boundaries and actual alternating inset. No human approval implied.
Read all 44 verses from enlarged source images and prepared first-pass encoding.

lg.label: XII.
lg.l: Quis fuit ille dies, quo tristia semper amanti
Omina non albae concinuistis aves?
Quodve putem sidus nostris occurrere fatis,
Quosve deos in me bella movere querar?
Quae modo dicta meast, quam coepi solus amare,
Cum multis vereor ne sit habenda mihi.
Fallimur, an nostris innotuit illa libellis?
Sic erit: ingenio prostitit illa meo.
Et merito! quid enim formae praeconia feci?
Vendibilis culpa facta puella meast.
Me lenone placet, duce me perductus amator,
Ianua per nostras est adaperta manus.
An prosint, dubium, nocuerunt carmina semper:
Invidiae nostris illa fuere bonis.
Cum Thebe, cum Troia foret, cum Caesaris acta,
Ingenium movit sola Corinna meum:
Aversis utinam tetigissem carmina Musis,
Phoebus et inceptum destituisset opus!
Nec tamen ut testes mos est audire poetas;
Malueram verbis pondus abesse meis.
Per nos Scylla patri caros furata capillos
Pube premit rapidos inguinibusque canes;
Nos pedibus pinnas dedimus, nos crinibus angues;
Victor Abantiades alite fertur equo.
Idem per spatium Tityon porreximus ingens,
Et tria vipereo fecimus ora cani;
* Fecimus Enceladon iaculantem mille lacertis,
Ambiguae captos virginis ore viros;
Aeolios Ithacis inclusimus utribus Euros;
Proditor in medio Tantalus amne sitit;
De Niobe silicem, de virgine fecimus ursam;
Concinit Odrysium Cecropis ales Ityn;
Iuppiter aut in aves aut se transformat in aurum
Aut secat inposita virgine taurus aquas;
Protea quid referam Thebanaque semina, dentes;
Qui vomerent flammas ore, fuisse boves,
Flere genis electra tuas, Auriga, sorores,
Quaeque rates fuerint, nunc maris esse deas,
Aversumque diem mensis furialibus Atrei
Duraque percussam saxa secuta lyram?
Exit in immensum fecunda licentia vatum,
Obligat historica nec sua verba fide;
Et mea debuerat falso laudata videri
Femina: credulitas nunc mihi vestra nocet.

div.head: Transcription notes
div.note: Heading XII. appears to the left of the opening verse. Both full printed pages show the alternating insets recorded explicitly here.
There is no comma after Omina; the verse ends with a question mark.
The printed contraction meast is retained, here and in verse10.
The source prints prostitit and a colon after erit. No alternative wording is supplied.
An exclamation mark follows merito; quid starts with lowercase q.
Commas surround dubium and a colon ends the verse.
The source proper-name forms are Thebe, Troia and Caesaris; they are retained.
The enlarged source shows a semicolon after poetas, not a colon; the next verse ends with a period.
The source spelling is Abantiades, retained as printed.
The source has Tityon with final n, followed later by porreximus ingens and a comma.

A printed asterisk stands to the left of Fecimus. It is retained as a separate metamark with unspecified function; the visible mark alone is not treated as a manuscript deletion or a reconstructed critical apparatus. The source name is Enceladon.
The verse ends in a semicolon. Below it the page carries OVID. I. and a separate signature5; these are encoded as forme work and do not become verse text.
The new page begins Aeolios Ithacis inclusimus utribus Euros; all proper-name spelling and the final semicolon are retained.
The source prints Odrysium Cecropis ales Ityn; no name or case ending is normalized.
The spelling inposita is retained with n before p.
A comma precedes dentes and a semicolon ends the verse. The next three verses end with commas; the final question mark occurs at40.
The final verse prints Femina: with a colon and credulitas with lowercase c; a period follows nocet. The next source heading XIII. establishes the boundary.
